questions.question: The charge to mass ratio of electron was found to be:
questions.explanation: Thomson’s experiments with cathode rays measured the electron’s e/m ratio at about 1.758 × 10¹¹ C kg^–1. Balancing electric and magnetic fields on the electron beam yields this value. Once the electron’s charge (1.602 × 10^–19 C) was known (Millikan’s oil-drop experiment), its mass (9.109 × 10^–31 kg) was determined.

questions.question: When -rays strike a thin gold foil then:
options: Most of the -rays do not pass through the gold foil.
Most of the -rays get deflected back.
Most of the -rays get deflected through small angles.
Most of the -rays pass through without any deviation.
questions.explanation: Rutherford’s gold-foil experiment showed that nearly all α-particles traveled straight through because the atom is mostly empty space. Only a small fraction were deflected at small angles, and an extremely small number were deflected back, indicating the presence of a tiny, dense, positively charged nucleus at the center.

questions.question: The number of neutrons present in deuterium is:
questions.explanation: Deuterium (²H) is an isotope of hydrogen having mass number 2. Since its nucleus contains one proton (atomic number 1), it must have one neutron: 2 (mass number) − 1 (proton) = 1 neutron.

questions.question: Metal of which foil was used in Rutherford experiment?
questions.explanation: Rutherford used a very thin gold foil in his famous α‑ray scattering experiment. Gold’s malleability allows it to be beaten into extremely thin sheets, enabling most α‑particles to pass through relatively easily and reveal how the atom’s positive charge is concentrated in a tiny nucleus.

questions.question: Which is true?
options: {e} / {m} values of cathode rays generated by discharge of different gases are different
({e} / {m}) value of anode rays generated by discharge of different gases is same
questions.explanation: Cathode rays (electrons) have the same e/m regardless of the gas, so (A) is incorrect. Anode (canal) rays’ e/m changes with different gases, so (B) is incorrect. Electron’s e/m is much larger than proton’s, so (C) is incorrect. Proton’s e/m exceeds that of an α‑particle, since the α‑particle has double the charge but quadruple the mass. Hence (D) is true.

hi.question: सत्य क्या है?
options: {e} / {m} विभिन्न गैसों के विसर्जन से उत्पन्न कैथोड किरणों के मान भिन्न होते हैं
({e} / {m}) विभिन्न गैसों के विसर्जन से उत्पन्न ऐनोड किरणों का मान समान होता है
hi.explanation: कैथोड किरणों (इलेक्ट्रॉनों) का e/m गैस की परवाह किए बिना समान होता है, इसलिए (A) गलत है।विभिन्न गैसों के साथ ऐनोड (नहर) किरणों का e/m बदलता है, इसलिए (B) गलत है।इलेक्ट्रॉन का e/m प्रोटॉन के e/m से बहुत अधिक होता है, इसलिए (C) गलत है।प्रोटॉन का e/m α-कण के e/m से अधिक होता है, क्योंकि α-कण पर आवेश दोगुना, लेकिन द्रव्यमान चार गुना होता है। अतः (D) सत्य है।

questions.question: When a gold sheet is bombarded by a beam of - particles, only a few of them get deflected whereas most go straight, undeflected. This is because
options: The force of attraction exerted on the - particles by the oppositely charged electrons is not sufficient.
A nucleus has a much smaller volume than that of an atom.
The force of repulsion acting on the fast moving -particles is very small.
The neutrons in the nucleus do not have any effect on the -particles.
questions.explanation: In Rutherford’s experiment, most α‑particles pass through the largely empty space around the nucleus. Only those particles that come very close to the tiny but massive nucleus get significantly deflected. Hence, only a small fraction undergo deflection, while the majority travel straight through.

questions.question: Rutherford's scattering experiment is related to the size of the
questions.explanation: Rutherford’s α‑particle scattering experiment showed that most of an atom’s mass and positive charge is concentrated in a very small central region (the nucleus). This helped establish that the nucleus is extremely small compared to the overall size of the atom.

questions.question: Rutherford in his atomic model could not explain the behavior of which of the following ?
The particles which were deflected backward in Rutherfords experiment were hit upon by:
questions.explanation: In Rutherford’s alpha-scattering experiment, a small fraction of α‑particles got deflected backward because they encountered the positively charged, massive and dense nucleus. They practically bounced back upon near-direct collision with the nucleus, since the nucleus contains most of the atom’s mass and has a high positive charge, causing strong electrostatic repulsion.

hi.question: रदरफोर्ड के प्रयोग में जो कण पीछे की और विक्षेपित हुए थे, वे किससे टकराए थे?
hi.explanation: रदरफोर्ड के प्रयोग में जो α-कण पीछे की ओर विक्षेपित हुए थे, वे परमाणु के नाभिक से टकराए थे। चूँकि नाभिक धनावेश युक्त और अत्यंत घना होता है, इसलिए जब कोई α-कण सीधे नाभिक से टकराता है या उसके बहुत समीप से गुजरता है, तो वह तीव्र कोण पर विक्षेपित हो जाता है। सही विकल्प है: A — नाभिक

questions.question: What did Rutherford conclude from his gold foil experiment?
options: Alpha particles are much smaller than gold atoms.
Radius of the nucleus is about 105 times less than the radius of the atom
No Alpha-particles passed through the gold foil.
questions.explanation: (Radius of the nucleus is about 10⁵ times less than the radius of the atom) Rutherford observed that most α‑particles passed straight through the thin gold foil, implying that atoms are mostly empty space. A small fraction was deflected sharply, indicating a tiny, massive, positively charged nucleus. From the scattering data, Rutherford concluded the nucleus is about 10⁵ times smaller in radius than the entire atom.

hi.question: रदरफोर्ड ने अपने सोने की पन्नी के प्रयोग से क्या निष्कर्ष निकाला?
options: α-कण सोने के परमाणुओ से बहुत छोटे होते है।
α-कण दोहरे आवेश वाले हीलियम आयन है।
नाभिक की त्रिज्या परमाणु की त्रिज्या से लगभग 105 गुना कम है
कोई α-कण सोने की पन्नी से होकर नहीं गुजरे
hi.explanation: रदरफोर्ड ने अपने प्रसिद्ध सोने की पन्नी वाले प्रयोग से यह महत्वपूर्ण निष्कर्ष निकाला कि परमाणु का अधिकांश भाग रिक्त होता है और उसका धनावेश नाभिक में केंद्रित होता है, जो परमाणु के आकार की तुलना में अत्यंत छोटा होता है। उन्होंने यह पाया कि अधिकांश α-कण बिना किसी विक्षेपण के पन्नी से सीधे निकल गए, जबकि कुछ ही α-कण थोड़े कोण पर मुड़ गए और बहुत ही कम α-कण तीव्र कोण पर परावर्तित हुए। इस अवलोकन से उन्होंने यह निष्कर्ष निकाला कि परमाणु के केंद्र में एक घना, धनावेश युक्त नाभिक होता है जिसकी त्रिज्या परमाणु की त्रिज्या से लगभग 10⁵ गुना कम होती है। यह खोज परमाणु संरचना की समझ में एक क्रांतिकारी कदम था और इसने थॉमसन के प्लम-पुडिंग मॉडल को अस्वीकार कर दिया।

questions.explanation: In the electromagnetic spectrum, radio waves have the longest wavelength, followed by microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X‑rays, γ‑rays, and finally cosmic rays with the shortest wavelengths.

questions.explanation: In the electromagnetic spectrum, cosmic rays possess the highest frequency (and thus the shortest wavelength) among the listed radiations, exceeding even γ‑rays. On the other end, radio waves have the lowest frequency (longest wavelength).

questions.question: Which is not characteristic of Planck's quantum theory of radiation?
options: Energy is not absorbed or emitted in whole number or multiples of quantum.
The magnitude of energy associated with a quantum is proportional to the frequency.
Radiation energy is neither emitted nor absorbed continuously but in small packets called quanta.
questions.explanation: Planck’s quantum theory states that energy is absorbed or emitted in integer multiples (whole numbers) of a basic quantum (hνh). Hence the statement “Energy is not absorbed or emitted in whole number or multiples of quantum” is incorrect and not a feature of Planck’s theory.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of Planck's quantum theory of radiation?
options: Energy is not absorbed or emitted in whole number integral multiples of quantum.
Radiation is associated with energy emitted or absorbed continuously but in the form of small packets called quanta
The magnitude of energy associated with quantum is proportional to frequency.
questions.explanation: Planck’s quantum theory states that radiation is emitted or absorbed in integral multiples of a fundamental quantum of energy (hν). Therefore, the statement that “Energy is not absorbed or emitted in whole number integral multiples of quantum” is not a characteristic of Planck’s theory.

questions.question: Light of wavelength strikes on a metal surface with intensity {X} and metal emits {Y} electrons per second of average energy Z . What will happen to Y and {Z} if {X} is doubled?

Both {Z} and Y will remain constant
{Z} will decrease and Y will increase
questions.explanation: With the same wavelength (λ), each photon’s energy (and thus the average electron energy ZZ) remains unchanged. However, doubling intensity doubles the number of incident photons per second, so the emission rate (YY) of photoelectrons doubles. Hence ZZ stays constant, YY increases.

questions.question: Which is the correct graphical representation based on photoelectric effect? (I) (II) (III) (IV)
questions.explanation: (II) K.E. vs Frequency: The photoelectron’s kinetic energy increases linearly with frequency (above the threshold); hence a rising straight line is correct. (IV) Number of photons (and thus number of photoelectrons) vs Intensity: This is a direct proportion, so a rising line is correct. By contrast, K.E. does not depend on intensity, so (III) is incorrect, and (I) is not the right shape for K.E. vs frequency.

questions.question: A certain metal when irradiated with light ({v}=3.2 .10¹⁶ {~Hz}) emits photo electrons with twice kinetic energy as did photoelectrons when the same metal is irradiated by light ({v}=2.0 10¹⁶ {~Hz}) . Calculate {v}_{0} of electron?
In the emission of photoelectrons, the number of photoelectrons emitted per unit time depends upon
questions.explanation: B. intensity of the incident radiation In the photoelectric effect, when light (or any electromagnetic radiation) falls on a metal surface: The energy of individual photoelectrons depends on the frequency of the incident radiation (related to the photon energy E=hνE = h). But, the number of photoelectrons emitted per unit time depends on the intensity of the incident light, provided the frequency is above the threshold frequency. Intensity means the number of photons falling per unit area per unit time. More photons = more chances of knocking out electrons.
